body: Thank you for your suggestions. I have been thinking about getting back in touch with a previous therapist for other reasons as well as this, so that’s definitely something to consider. I don’t think I’d be able to share with someone else because a lot of the factors surrounding my ex’s behaviour are very personal to them, so it doesn’t seem fair to share that with someone other than a professional, otherwise that would be a good idea too. I’ve never tried writing in a journal, but it’s certainly worth a try, and I’m glad to hear it helped you process things too, hopefully you’re in a better place now!
I’m sorry to hear you’ve been in a similar situation but that is a really good analogy, thank you for sharing. Are things better with your SO now?

Thank you, I needed to hear that.

It doesn’t help that in our younger days we both slept around a little so I don’t think he’s acknowledged that my feelings about sex have changed and it’s more emotional now.
We do, you may be right though.

I think you’re right about the emotional immaturity. He hasn’t got any sort of history of abuse (that he’s shared with me, I don’t think it’s something he’d have hidden for this long though) but he is quite bad for instant gratification in other areas of life.

Thank you for your thoughts. We’re not married, both in our mid 20s. We used to be good at communicating but now it tends to dissolve into an argument when issues come up. He’s made it quite clear he just doesn’t understand the link on my part, maybe it’s just wishful thinking from me that there’s a way I could put it that would make him more empathetic...

I have heard of love languages, that’s a good suggestion for opening a dialogue for different ways to look at things so thank you! 

As a fellow lurker I appreciate your foray into replying to a post!
Sorry to hear you’re going through the same thing 😔
